description: Composite figure of Charpy impact fracture surfaces mixing six panels of two kinds. (a–c) are low-magnification macrographs of whole fracture surfaces of the Fe-20Mn-6Al-0.6C-0.15Si low-density steel tested at (a) −196 °C, (b) −77 °C and (c) RT; each carries a 1 mm scale bar, a "V-notch" label along the top, yellow arrow labels for "radial zone" and "shear lip", and a colour-coded 3D topography map inset at the lower left whose axes are unreadable. In (b) and (c) a dashed yellow line outlines a "fibrous zone" that is not outlined in (a) and is visibly larger in (c) than in (b). (d–f) are secondary-electron SEM images of the radial zone: (d) at −196 °C (100 µm scale bar) with arrows marking "large dimples", "tear edges" and "dimples"; (e) at −77 °C (20 µm scale bar) and (f) at RT (20 µm scale bar), both labelled "dimples", with (f) showing the largest, most equiaxed dimples. Taken together the panels argue that the −196 °C surface is markedly flatter with high-density large dimples and tear edges (quasi-cleavage), whereas −77 °C and RT show progressively more pronounced dimple-type ductile fracture. Caption: (a,d) −196 °C; (b,e) −77 °C; (c,f) RT.
measured_quantities: impact absorbed energy W_all (J, reported in citing text only)

observations.observation: Panels (a–c) are low-magnification macrographs of whole Charpy fracture surfaces, each with a 1 mm scale bar and the labels 'V-notch', 'radial zone' and 'shear lip' printed in yellow.
A yellow arrow labelled 'shear lip' marks a shear lip on the right-hand edge of the fracture surface in (a), (b) and (c), i.e. at all three test temperatures.
A dashed yellow outline labelled 'fibrous zone' is drawn in (b) and (c) but not in (a); the outlined region is visibly larger in (c) (RT) than in (b) (−77 °C).

Each of (a–c) contains a colour-coded 3D topography map inset at the lower left; the inset surface in (a) appears flatter while the insets in (b) and (c) show greater relief, but the inset axis numbers and colour scale are unreadable at the supplied resolution.
Panel (d) is an SEM image with a 100 µm scale bar whose arrows label 'large dimples', 'tear edges' and 'dimples', indicating a finer-scale view than (e) and (f) which use 20 µm scale bars.
Panels (e) and (f) are SEM images with 20 µm scale bars whose only printed label is 'dimples'; (f) (RT) shows markedly larger and more equiaxed dimples than (e).
The caption maps the panels to test temperatures: (a,d) −196 °C; (b,e) −77 °C; (c,f) RT.
The citing text states that shear lips are present on the fracture surfaces of all samples (Fig. 6a–c) independent of test temperature, indicating ductile fracture.
The citing text states that almost no fibrous zone is observed at −196 °C while a larger fibrous zone appears at −77 °C and RT, suggesting better toughness at −77 °C and RT.
The citing text states that the 3D topography maps inserted in Fig. 6a–c show the −196 °C fracture surface to be significantly flatter than the others.

The citing text states that at −196 °C the sample displayed a combination of ductile and brittle fracture, with high-density large dimples and tear edges as marked in Fig. 6d indicating a tendency to quasi-cleavage cracks.
The citing text reports a relatively low W_all of 188 J for the sample tested at −196 °C; this value is not printed anywhere in the figure itself.
The citing text states that all samples were compressed, reducing fracture surface area, and that this becomes more pronounced as temperature increases.

subfigures.description: Macrograph of the fracture surface of the impact sample tested at −196 °C (1 mm scale bar); labels 'V-notch' (top), 'radial zone' (arrow, centre) and 'shear lip' (arrow, right). A colour-coded 3D topography map is inset at lower left, showing a comparatively flat surface; its axis values are unreadable.

Macrograph of the fracture surface at −77 °C (1 mm scale bar); 'V-notch', 'radial zone' and 'shear lip' labelled, plus a dashed yellow outline delimiting a 'fibrous zone' just below the notch. A 3D topography map inset sits at lower left.

Macrograph of the fracture surface at RT (1 mm scale bar); same labels ('V-notch', 'fibrous zone' enclosed by dashed yellow line, 'radial zone', 'shear lip'). The outlined fibrous zone is larger than in (b). 3D topography map inset at lower left.
SEM image of the radial zone of the −196 °C sample (100 µm scale bar) with labelled arrows for 'large dimples', 'tear edges' and 'dimples'; high-density large dimples and tear edges are visible.
SEM image of the −77 °C sample (20 µm scale bar) labelled 'dimples'; a dimple/tear-ridge network is visible. A second yellow arrow at the top points off-frame with no legible label.
SEM image of the RT sample (20 µm scale bar) labelled 'dimples'; large, deep equiaxed dimples with raised rims dominate the field.
